title: Piano Sonata No. 3 in B minor
hook: Chopin’s last piano sonata, with a slow movement like a night song and a finale that gallops into a major key.

painting.title: George Sand’s Garden at Nohant
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: The shady garden at Nohant, painted by Chopin’s friend Delacroix during his stays with Sand and Chopin there; Chopin wrote this sonata in the same house in the summer of 1844.

facts: Chopin wrote the sonata in the second half of 1844, much of it during the summer at Nohant, George Sand’s country house in central France. It was almost the only work he finished that year; his health was getting worse and he was composing less and less.
It was published in Paris in 1845 with a dedication to the Countess Élise de Perthuis, whose husband was an aide to King Louis-Philippe.
It is the last of his piano sonatas, and one of his hardest works to play. Unlike his Second Sonata, with its funeral march, it has a lyrical slow movement and ends in a major key.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a grand first movement full of ideas (I), a whirl of fast notes (II), a long night song (III), a galloping finale that ends in triumph (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro maestoso
movements.summary: A proud, falling phrase opens the movement, and one idea grows out of another in quick succession. Then comes one of Chopin’s most beautiful melodies, a long song in D major. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]], with a twist: when the themes return, the opening theme is left out, and the song comes back on its own, now in B major.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a bold, falling phrase in B minor, then a sequence of strong chords.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a long, calm melody in D major over a gently rocking left hand, like a [[nocturne|nocturne]].

mainIdeas.name: The closing theme
mainIdeas.description: soft, rippling figures that end the exposition quietly.

stops.hear: A proud phrase falls from high to low, followed by strong chords
New ideas follow one another: a march-like passage, voices weaving in and out
The music calms: a long, singing melody over a rocking accompaniment
Soft, rippling figures, slowing down
The proud falling phrase again, from the start
The opening phrase is broken up and set against itself in several voices
The long D major song returns, now in B major, without the proud opening theme

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: A firm, bright ending in B major

notice: Listen for what never comes back: the proud opening phrase is missing from the recapitulation. Chopin did the same in his Second Sonata.
In Theme 2, listen to the left hand. Its gentle rocking keeps going under the whole melody.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Argerich was 25. Two years earlier, in 1965, she had won the International Chopin Piano Competition in Warsaw.

movements.heading: Scherzo: Molto vivace
movements.summary: A very short [[scherzo|scherzo]]: a whirl of quick, light notes in the right hand, with only a few touches in the left. In the middle, a [[trio|trio]] slows down into a calm, hymn-like tune, then the whirl returns.

mainIdeas.name: The scherzo
mainIdeas.description: a continuous stream of fast notes, light and glittering.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: a quiet melody in the inner voices, held between long notes above and below.

stops.hear: The right hand races in a light, glittering stream of notes
Slower and quieter: a calm melody inside sustained chords
The fast, glittering stream returns

stops.label: Last 10 seconds
stops.hear: A last quick flourish

notice: Listen for the trio’s melody in the middle of the texture. It is surrounded by long, held notes, as if behind a veil.

movements.heading: Largo
movements.summary: After four loud bars in a stern, dotted rhythm, the music becomes a long, calm song in B major, close to a [[nocturne|nocturne]]. The middle section is much longer than the outer parts: slow, rippling figures in which time seems to stop. The song returns briefly and the movement ends in peace.

mainIdeas.name: The introduction
mainIdeas.description: four forceful bars in a dotted rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a slow, singing melody over a quiet, steady accompaniment.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: gentle, rippling broken chords in E major, like water at night.

stops.hear: A few loud, stern bars in a dotted rhythm
stops.happening: A short introduction, moving from the scherzo’s key to B major

stops.hear: A calm, singing melody, slow and tender
Gentle, rippling broken chords; the melody almost disappears into them
stops.happening: The long middle section, in E major

stops.hear: The singing melody returns
The song and the rippling figures meet, and the music fades

notice: Notice how long the middle section lasts: about three times as long as the opening song. Let yourself drift with it.

movements.heading: Finale: Presto non tanto
movements.summary: Eight loud bars in octaves, a pause, and the main theme gallops off over a running bass. The theme returns three times, each time with a faster, fuller accompaniment, between brilliant episodes in other keys. The sonata ends in B major, in triumph.

mainIdeas.name: The main theme
mainIdeas.description: an urgent, galloping tune over rolling triplets in the left hand.

mainIdeas.name: The episodes
mainIdeas.description: brilliant runs and bright major-key music between the returns.

stops.hear: Loud, heavy octaves in both hands, then a pause on a high note
An urgent, galloping tune over rolling notes in the left hand
stops.happening: The main theme, in B minor

stops.hear: Brilliant, racing runs in a major key
The galloping tune returns, now against a different rhythm in the left hand
stops.happening: The second statement, in E minor

stops.hear: The tune comes back once more, with an even faster accompaniment
stops.happening: The third statement, in B minor

stops.hear: The music turns to B major and drives to the end with full chords

notice: Follow the left hand each time the main theme returns. It moves faster every time, so the tune seems to gallop harder.

threads.title: Song inside the storm
threads.body: Every movement holds a song: the D major theme of the first, the trio of the scherzo, the whole Largo.

threads.title: Rules bent
threads.body: As in his Second Sonata, Chopin leaves the main theme out of the first movement’s recapitulation.

threads.title: From dark to light
threads.body: The sonata begins in B minor and ends in B major. His Second Sonata ended in a whisper; this one ends in triumph.
